card_pick.why: The only fit the ledger and the installed package leave open. slide is BLOCKED (every-job). book-flip and swap are fresh, but @remotion/transitions 4.0.462 in video-creation/remotion ships neither (dist/presentations: clock-wipe, fade, flip, iris, none, slide, wipe, zoom-blur, zoom-in-out) and both need Chrome's canvas-draw-element flag; cube has no rmn: presentation (comp-build section 6, it would be hand:cube-3d) and sits in the last three anyway. flip is recent (golden-kitty, two videos back), so the usage check WARNs, never FAILs. Fit: a token rundown is a stack of four cards, one per coin, and a card turning over to the next token is the list's own gesture. Direction from-right on all four (the list reads forward, and the corner-ease spins lead with the right edge too). Timing as the EDIT-PLAN carved it: CH2 flips in at the pause (104.99, readable about 1.10 s); CH3, CH4 and CH5 flip in ON the face-out frame (268.033, 371.733, 494.900; readable about 1.34, 1.17 and 1.13 s). The card lands 12 frames in with the DSGNImpt peak on that frame, holds through the 1.5 s pause, and flips out onto the chapter's first visual over 10 frames as the pause ends, so readability never drops under 1 s. Self-contained card scene; the spine is never wrapped in TransitionSeries.

face_glitch_pick.why: Film burn over the Blocks glitch, by register: a gear-2 explainer on subtle beds where Mike capped the sound design at one soft card impact; a warm optical flash suits that, a digital block shatter on 20 edges does not. The advisory ledger agrees (Blocks on the previous video, film burn two back). With the 22 library light leaks inside the windows the face becomes one optical film language (burn on the edges, leak on the joins), and the only digital texture left is the AI-still roll. Standard burn 0.76 s on 15 edges; the SHORT burn 0.40 s on 5: F4's two edges (a 1.63 s window) and the three face outs a title card turns over (268.033, 371.733, 494.900), where the flip carries the exit and the burn only flashes the seam. The F11 picture end (648.267) is a plain hand:cut. An overlay peaking on the cut, so no frozen face node is needed except the card scenes' faithful last-frame freeze (comp-build section 6a).

ai_still_pick.why: Advisory slot: TV Satellite carried the previous video, Turbulent Displace and Cinematic Bad Signal the ones before; Offset is fresh and the quietest glitch that still reads as one: a v-sync roll bump with red / green edge fringes, no noise plate, no strobe, so it marks each ChatGPT image as an illustration without shouting over a gear-2 explainer (Monitor, VHS and Invert read broken-TV, retro or strobing; Blocks was the face look of four earlier videos). It is the one family with no pack SFX, which matches Mike's muted-SFX ruling exactly, and a geometric engine (no plates to copy). Two tiers of the one look: 1x (0.40 s) on 13 explainer stills, 2x (0.48 s) on 5 (IMG-1, the first still, and the four chapter-thesis images IMG-7, IMG-13, IMG-16, IMG-21). 18 ingresses; IMG-4 is face-owned, IMG-5, IMG-10 and IMG-14 are card-owned.

face_leak_pick.why: Ledger slot face_leak: the previous video's lightleaks-2 / -5 / -short-2 / -short-5 are BLOCKED; all four picks are fresh. Two plates, each in its full and short cut: lightleaks-8 (orange, warm) and lightleaks-3 (blue / magenta, cool), energy medium, an organic film flash that sits beside the film-burn edges. The cycle follows the punch itself: the warm plate on every step IN, the cool plate on every step BACK, so each window opens warm and the alternation reads as breathing. Full 1.12 s plates (peak 0.32 s in) on the 17 joins with room; the 0.40 s short cuts (peak 0.16 s in) on the 5 joins within 0.8 s of a face-out burn or the as-filmed cut (371.2, 419.9, 494.233, 571.067, 587.467), so no frame carries both a leak and a burn. The soft looks (1.44 s) were passed over: their long tail overlaps the 28.967 join and the F5-out burn. Screen blend, under the captions, baked SFX muted.

melt_pick.why: The only melt look open: MELT/RGB is BLOCKED (every-job) and PROJECT-LOG records no waiver. MELT/Equidistant was golden-kitty's (two videos back), so the usage check WARNs. It fits TRANSFORM: the frame wraps into a spherical vortex and the next structure unwinds out of it, the clearest picture of one thing reflowing into another. Full 0.84 s only (energy medium, the gear-2 tier; the 0.44 s short ids are energy high and a second family to the lint, never mixed). Two ids of the one look, direction by context: melt-equidistant-1 (tilt down) and melt-equidistant-2 (tilt up). The engine is image-only: both uses are planned still to still through TransitionClip's fromSrc / toSrc (the passthrough and the paint fix golden-kitty needed are now in the engine and the wrapper). kind:shader, full-frame warp, the spine never peeks; baked SFX ducked, in practice MUTED.

spin_pick.why: Fresh on the ledger (SPIN/3D Corner Ease is BLOCKED; 3D Side Ease and 3D Center Ease are in the last three). Of the seven fresh looks it is the one that reads as turning to a new facet rather than as an effect: a flat corner-hinged swing where the outgoing board rotates away about a frame corner and the next board swings in and eases to rest. Bounce, Swinging and Shake read playful against a gear-2 explainer, Center Ease whips, and Twirl's vortex would blur into the Equidistant melt. One exact id on all four uses, spin-corner-ease-lt: hinged on the top-left corner, the next board drops in with its right edge settling last, the same right-leading motion as the from-right card flip, so card and spin share one hinge language. Full 0.76 s (the lint reads the -short ids as a second look). kind:geometric over mirrored padding: full-frame mid-swing, occlusion safe; baked SFX ducked, in practice MUTED.
